Review n8n?

Reviewers largely see n8n as a powerful, flexible automation tool that shines once you get past the learning curve. Users repeatedly praise its visual workflow builder, strong API handling, self-hosting, privacy control, and ability to manage complex multi-step logic that feels limiting in Zapier or Make. Several say it is reliable and easier to read and debug than script-heavy setups. The main complaints are a steep setup and onboarding experience, gaps in some native integrations, and a few concerns around scaling, version control, and how open-source it feels.

#### What's great

n8n is not the best workflow engine ever built, but it is probably the best compromise between developer flexibility, speed of development, self-hosting, and operational complexity. For teams between "simple automations" and "full microservice orchestration," it's in a very strong position.

Cristiano Ortolani

#### What's great

I’ve been using n8n for a while, and it’s incredible to see how far it’s come. The flexibility and self-hosting options make it stand out compared to other automation tools. It’s become an essential part of my workflow — especially for connecting internal services and APIs in a privacy-friendly way. Congrats to the team for continuously improving an open and developer-friendly platform!

#### What's great

The backend glue that keeps a small company running is usually a pile of half-documented scripts nobody wants to touch, and n8n is the first tool that made me comfortable handing that job to something visual instead.

Connecting the tools we already use, without writing a script for each one, is where the time savings actually show up.

The workflow builder reads like a flowchart, so tracing why something didn't fire is a five-minute job instead of digging through logs.
